feed.title: Microsoft Teams Platform
feed.subtitle: Updated articles for Microsoft Teams Platform

entry.title: Preview: Extended Markdown formatting for agent messages
entry.summary:
Agents can now send richer, better-formatted responses using extended Markdown formatting (currently in preview), supporting tables, task lists, code blocks, equations, images, at-mentions, and citations. Extended Markdown content renders progressively during streaming.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: Teams SDK for Python hotfix
entry.summary:
Hotfix releases for both the stable (2.0.16) and preview (2.1.0a2) tracks of Teams SDK for Python are now available on PyPI.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: Teams SDK (stable and preview, multiple languages)
entry.summary:
New versions of Teams SDK are now available across TypeScript, .NET, and Python, including stable maintenance releases and preview support for Agent 365 scenarios. Teams SDK for .NET 2.1.0 also introduces an ASP.NET Core application model, agentic identity, multi-flow OAuth, built-in state, OpenTelemetry, and Bot Framework v4 compatibility.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Retiring: App manifest environment variables
entry.summary:
The Teams Developer Portal's environment variables feature for app manifests will be retired on August 31, 2026, after which manifests that use environment variables will become invalid and the variables will no longer be available for creation, management, or access. Apps that rely on this feature should be split into per-environment apps before the retirement date.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: New admin controls for meeting transcripts
entry.summary:
New controls governing access to meeting transcripts are now generally available to tenant administrators in Teams Admin Center, including options to deny all transcript access through the Graph API or allow access only to transcripts without speaker attribution. Developers should clearly communicate transcript access requirements, handle denied access, and support non-attributed transcript formats.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: Targeted messages and agent slash commands
entry.summary:
Targeted messaging and agent slash commands are now generally available, enabling private user-to-agent messages in group conversations and named commands that users can activate from chat. App manifest updates are required to register agent slash commands and enable targeted messages for an agent.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: Emoji chat reactions for agents
entry.summary:
Emoji chat reactions for agents are now generally available, allowing agents to add and remove reactions to messages in a chat to communicate acknowledgement, status, and other information in a lightweight way.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Released: Apps in private channels
entry.summary:
Support for agent and app participation in private channels is now generally available. Implementing this capability requires consideration of the agent implementation and app manifest configuration for private channel operation.

For more information, see the announcement.

entry.title: Coming soon: New admin controls for meeting transcripts
entry.summary:
New controls governing access to meeting transcripts have entered public preview, allowing administrators to deny all transcript access through the Graph API or restrict access to transcripts without speaker attribution.

For more information, see the announcement.
